text_blocks.snippet: Severe gum disease, also known as periodontitis, requires professional treatment to prevent further damage to the gums and supporting bone. Treatment options range from deep cleaning procedures (scaling and root planing) to surgical interventions like flap surgery, bone grafting, and guided tissue regeneration. Antibiotics may also be used to control bacterial infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: deep cleaning procedures (scaling and root planing) to surgical interventions like flap surgery, bone grafting, and guided tissue regeneration

list.title: Scaling and Root Planing:
list.snippet: This deep cleaning procedure removes plaque and tartar from above and below the gum line, smoothing the tooth roots to prevent bacterial buildup.

list.title: Medications:
list.snippet: Antibiotics, either as a rinse or slow-release chip, can help reduce bacteria and inflammation.

list.title: Flap Surgery (Pocket Reduction Surgery):
list.snippet: This procedure involves lifting the gums, removing bacteria and tartar, and smoothing the underlying bone before suturing the gums back into place.

list.title: Bone Grafting:
list.snippet: If bone loss has occurred, bone grafting can help regenerate lost bone and support the teeth.

list.title: Guided Tissue Regeneration:
list.snippet: This technique uses a mesh-like material to encourage the growth of bone and gum tissue.

list.title: Gingivectomy:
list.snippet: In cases of excessive gum tissue, a gingivectomy removes the excess tissue and reshapes the gum line.

list.title: Laser Treatment:
list.snippet: Lasers can be used to remove diseased tissue and bacteria in some cases, potentially offering a less invasive alternative to traditional surgery, says the Golden Triangle Periodontal Center.

list.title: Maintenance:
list.snippet: Regular follow-up appointments with a periodontist are crucial to monitor progress and prevent recurrence.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: It's essential to consult with a dentist or periodontist to determine the most appropriate treatment plan for your specific case of severe gum disease, says UT Health San Antonio.
